newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RESEARCH ALERT - HLG downgrades DCB to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - HLG downgrades DCB to hold.

text.p: HLG Securities said on Thursday it was downgrading the stock of financial group DCB Holdings Bhd (DCB) to a hold from buy, due to uncertainties over its restructuring.
In a research note, HLG said speculation that Rashid Hussain Securities, a unit of Rashid Hussain Bhd, may be acquired by DCB weighed on the stock.

"If the rumoured acquisition of Rashid Hussain Securities materialises, the benefits to DCB are mixed depending on the purchase price, while there are apparently not much further synergies to be enjoyed from the marriage.
"There is also a danger that DCB's valuations may be rerated downward as stockbroking income trades on lower PERs (price-to-earning ratio)," HLG said.
Rashid Hussain stock has climbed strongly in the last few weeks on a number of rumours.
These include talk linking it to DCB's restructuring, privatisation of Malaysia's second largest bank Bank Bumiputra Malaysia Bhd to Rashid, and a stake acquisition by a U.S. investment bank.
There has also been talk of Rashid acquiring other financial groups which may be injected into DCB.
Rashid Hussain holds a 20.3 percent stake in DCB, Malaysia's fifth largest banking group.
DCB and Rashid officials have declined to comment on the speculation.

A long-rumoured merger between DCB, Bank Bumiputra and financial group Commerce Asset-Holdings Bhd (CAHB) "is seen more positively because if it materialises, a dynamic and competitive institution would arise," HLG said.
But HLG said it may be premature to bank on the rumoured merger of the three institutions.
"The question of ownership and control of the merged entity has to be overcome and this is likely to be sticky. It is also cheaper to buy CAHB for the rumoured merger than DCB," HLG said.
